ubuntu.label: 26.04 LTS "Resolute Raccoon" (current LTS)
notes: Ubuntu 26.04 raised the desktop minimum to 6 GB RAM (it was 4 GB). With 4 GB or less, use Ubuntu Server and add a light desktop, or pick a lighter flavour such as Lubuntu.
The 26.04 desktop is Wayland only (no X11 session), which matters for some NVIDIA setups and older remote-desktop tools.
ubuntu.checked_note: minimum RAM, disk and support end date

ubuntu.label: 26.10 "Stonking Stingray" (interim, 9 months)
notes: Interim release: it gets updates for only about 9 months, so you must upgrade again in 2027. Choose 26.04 LTS for anything long-lived.
Requirements are assumed to match 26.04 LTS; they were not separately confirmed.

Reported change (one source, check the 26.10 release notes): with Secure Boot on, the signed GRUB can no longer read Btrfs, XFS or ZFS, nor LVM, software RAID or LUKS. Keep /boot (or the whole root) on plain ext4 if Secure Boot is enabled.
ubuntu.checked_note: release date and support end date

ubuntu.label: 24.04 LTS "Noble Numbat" (previous LTS)
notes: A good choice if your PC has 4 GB of RAM and cannot meet the 26.04 minimum.

ubuntu.label: Server 26.04 LTS (text installer)

install_steps: Boot the Ubuntu Server ISO. It starts the text installer.
Choose language and keyboard layout, then the installation type (Ubuntu Server or the minimized option).
Configure the network and, if needed, a proxy or mirror.
At Storage choose 'Custom storage layout' to apply the layout above, or 'Use an entire disk' (optionally with LVM). Review the summary before confirming.
Set the server name and create a user. Enable the OpenSSH server if you will manage it remotely, and pick any optional snaps.
Install, then reboot and remove the USB stick when asked.

notes: Server requirements start at 1.5 GB RAM and 4 GB storage and grow with what you run on it.
ubuntu.checked_note: minimum RAM, disk and support end date

opensuse.label: Leap 16.0 (stable)

install_steps: Boot the openSUSE installer image. It starts Agama, a web-based installer, in a live environment (you can also open it from another computer on the same network).
Choose language and keyboard, then pick the product to install (Leap 16.0 or Tumbleweed; both come from the same image).
On the overview page open the storage section. Choose the target disk, then use the custom/advanced option to apply the layout above, or accept the proposal (Btrfs root with snapshots).
Set the root user and create a user account, then open the software section to choose a desktop pattern.
Check the overview page one last time, click Install, then reboot and remove the USB stick.

notes: Leap 16 requires a CPU with x86-64-v2 (most processors since about 2008). Older machines should use Tumbleweed or Slowroll.
Leap 16 dropped 32-bit support, replaced YaST's installer with Agama, and enables SELinux by default.
opensuse.checked_note: installer, CPU requirement and support period

opensuse.label: Tumbleweed (rolling)

install_steps: Boot the openSUSE installer image. It starts Agama, a web-based installer, in a live environment (you can also open it from another computer on the same network).
Choose language and keyboard, then pick the product to install (Leap 16.0 or Tumbleweed; both come from the same image).
On the overview page open the storage section. Choose the target disk, then use the custom/advanced option to apply the layout above, or accept the proposal (Btrfs root with snapshots).
Set the root user and create a user account, then open the software section to choose a desktop pattern.
Check the overview page one last time, click Install, then reboot and remove the USB stick.

notes: Rolling release: always the newest software, with frequent updates. Run 'zypper dup' to update.
Slowroll is a middle option with slower, monthly-style updates.
